title: Leaf-fall rate: the abscission half of the economy retune
question: Pick the leaf-fall rate: at which arm does the floor stop reading as a giant soil pile before the canopy starts reading as overstuffed?
context_md:
Your verdict was: leaves fall too fast -> too much food and a giant pile of soil. The lever is `tree.ron`'s abscission pressure (a new counter attributes 88% of all leaf fall to `shade_death`; drought is 2%). Same scene, same seed, 12,000 frames, four tiles each; only the abscission rate differs.

- **A** current rate (0.003)
- **B** half (0.0015)
- **C** quarter (0.00075)

What the counters say: soil manufacture (decay events) falls 6,331 -> 3,443 -> 1,800, standing floor litter 1,081 -> 569 -> 321. One honest caveat: total colony-band food *energy* does not fall -- retained foliage means more low standing leaf within ant reach (medians 70k -> 82k -> 91k over 3 census seeds), so this lever fixes the floor, not total abundance. If what bothers you is the pile and the rot, B or C deliver it; if it is total food, say so and the next lever is different (leaf worth or canopy size, a separate card).

Crown separation held by eye at C (the risk was re-fused crowns, last measured breaking only at rate 0.0). Ignore the ants: wetland founding places 18 of 52 in every arm alike -- known scene behaviour, not part of this question. The 4x omnivore food-scale restoration already landed and is untouched here.
